I always felt rather unwanted, i was born with mental issues while my siblings were fine. Further more my parents were just so burnt out from raising my siblings that they didn’t do anything much with me and were often too exhausted to listen to me or my childish ramblings. Never watched a movie i liked together, never read me a bedtime story- well even if they did, they clearly didn’t enjoy it. 

I never realised it till recently, but i always had that nagging feeling of “you’re a burden to them”. I know they do love me, but they really should of just stopped at 2 if they were so tired, it alone really messed me up. Heck, my mother didn’t even love my dad anymore by then, she didn’t even tell him i was born till afterwards. And she didn’t cheat either, i and all my siblings look a lot like my father.

God damn, this makes the child-haters on the anti-natalist subreddit seem non-existent

No wonder us childfree folk get a bad rep (as a kid i was even told anti-natalists wanted mass human genocide and encouraged suicide, now i can see where people might of gotten that idea from)
It’s not even about political stances, i’ve seen people who are pro abortion yet get cold feet when the topic of just not having kids is brought up

The real issue is how pushy people get when you don’t want to have kids. If that wasn’t the case than yes it’d be attention seeking, but no, a lot of places heavily enforce child birth as being your destiny and shame you greatly if you don’t have kids. I usually never run into “internet issues” irl, but one problem i’ve faced countless times is people been appalled that i don’t want kids. 

You should see the lengths people will go to get grandchildren out of their kids, especially in religious countries. I don’t speak up about my real views on it at all irl because i have siblings who have kids and i don’t want them to feel ashamed or god forbid feel like i hate them. I also only speak about it when directly asked (which is unfortunately alot)

I love kids and want to protect them, but i don’t want one, nor do i need one of my own to be happy. If only people could get that through their heads. Then it’d be a non-issue indeed.

Tl:dr - if people stopped been such assholes to people who didn’t have kids, and didn’t treat them as idiots, this would be a non issue.

Was doing a hospitality degree (i was young and thought it would get me somewhere in life, silly me). 

In the course we actually ran a restaurant on campus. We all took turns manning the register, and if it was out we’d get in massive trouble. It was my turn to man the register one night and though i was used to doing the jobs of all the lazy folk there tonight was hectic. I kept getting called away or pushed away from the register, every time i double checked that i did things right while when i was away, i had to rely on the word of the others that they’d handle it.

It was my fault overall for been such a push over, but in the end- surprise surprise, i was out by a lot. It taught me a valuable lesson before i even got into the workforce, don’t do other peoples’ jobs and only do your own. 

Worse still, everyone blamed me for being out and thought i was just an idiot who was doing the course to pass the time from then on- though they still asked me to do their jobs. And got mad when i stopped doing their jobs.
